license_declaration.open_game_content: OGL 1.0a (Wizards of the Coast), inherited from the including core_rulebook.pcc per docs/governance/license-matrix.md §'Unestablished: 1 of 37'. core_essentials' own _core_essentials.pcc carries PUBNAMELONG:Paizo Inc. active but has every ISOGL:YES (line 16) and every COPYRIGHT: line (lines 19-) prefixed with '#' — commented out, not absent — so read alone it makes no active declaration. It is never loaded standalone in this corpus: core_rulebook.pcc line 43 reads PCC:@/pathfinder/paizo/roleplaying_game/core_essentials/_core_essentials.pcc, a direct unconditional inclusion, and Core Rulebook carries its own real active ISOGL:YES and COPYRIGHT block. This ingest reaches the two subrace files only through that same Core Rulebook inclusion path, which is the exact path the matrix rules recoverable.
license_declaration.product_identity_note: The 64 records this run wrote are Aasimar and Tiefling heritage (subrace) traits. 9 of 64 descriptions were redacted. Eight hit a blacklist term — the four Tiefling heritages named for outsider races that are Golarion Product Identity (Kyton-Spawn, Oni-Spawn, Devil-Spawn, Rakshasa-Spawn), each hit twice because the selector row and its Ability Scores replacement row repeat the same prose. **The ninth was restated 2026-08-12 (SD-29 `decisions.md` 53)**: `Tiefling ~ Daemon-Spawn` declares `DESCISPI:YES` — PCGen's own per-record statement that the description is Product Identity — and its prose ('tied to the daemons of Abaddon') names nothing the 55-term list knows, so the term scan alone published it. The row's declaration now governs. Aasimar's 24 records hit 0 terms and declare nothing. The identical screen ran over every field of every record.
license_declaration.product_identity_source: Paizo Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook, OGL §15 Product Identity section (core_essentials is distributed as part of that book's data set)

operator_sign_off.note: Set true only after an operator has reviewed this book's classification pass, per docs/governance/ogl-pi-blacklist.md's DRAFT header.

screening_method_note: Every field of the 64 heritage-trait records this run wrote was screened BOTH against the bounded, documented term list in docs/governance/ogl-pi-blacklist.md AND against the row's own `DESCISPI:YES`/`NAMEISPI:YES` declaration, by src/rules_core/pi_screening.rs, which the ingest binary calls per record. The two screens are a union, never a substitution. Verified on the written tree rather than assumed: `grep -rl 'redacted PI' data/corpus/core_essentials/race_trait/ | wc -l` -> 9, and records_processed is the real on-disk count (`find data/corpus/core_essentials/race_trait -name '*.json' | wc -l` -> 64). SCOPE NOTE: this declaration covers exactly the two files this book's BookSource lists — races/aasimar/aasimar_abilities_race_subrace.lst and races/tiefling/tiefling_abilities_race_subrace.lst — plus the two races/<race>/<race>_abilities_globalvar_subrace.lst files read for the swap protocol, which contribute gate structure and no prose. core_essentials' other racial-ability files are already ingested under the core_rulebook and beastiary book ids by src/bin/ingest_races.rs and are not re-declared here. races/skinwalker/ is out of scope: Skinwalker is not one of the 18 races this project models. This is NOT an exhaustive human legal review; it is a bounded substring scan and does not prove the absence of PI beyond what that scan can see.
